headline: Approved site plan waiver for BJs facility at 39 Gilmore Drive and Wedgewood Farm changes; recommended accessory dwelling unit bylaw to Town Meeting.
summary: Goods from BJs stores will be stored and re-palleted at 39 Gilmore Drive, with about 40 trucks leaving and returning each day. Wedgewood Farm will convert 9 triplexes to 8 duplexes and 7 singles and change two roadways to cul-de-sacs, after engineered plans are reviewed. The meeting also covered data centers, a Wilkinsonville Water District permit request, and truck concerns on Boston Road, which will be discussed at a later meeting.
decisions: Approved site plan waiver for 39 Gilmore Drive as a BJs cross-dock facility, 5-0, with conditions.
Recommended that Town Meeting approve the accessory dwelling unit (ADU) bylaw article, 5-0.
Approved waiver of the formal Site Plan Review hearing for Wedgewood Farm changes, 5-0, conditioned on engineered plans.

# SUTTON PLANNING BOARD

Meeting Minutes

September 14, 2026

Approved [signature]

W. Talcott read the following notice: Pursuant to Governor Healey's directive extending the temporary Open Meeting provisions until June 30, 2027, the Planning Board meeting will be conducted in a HYBRID format and will be recorded. *Any person in attendance making an audio or video recording of this meeting must notify the Chair at this time. *Recordings will be available on the Town's website and YouTube channel. *Please be aware: Participants attending via Zoom will have their video and audio disabled. *If you wish to engage in discussion, raise your hand; if the Chair acknowledges you, you will receive a pop-up message allowing you to unmute yourself. For agenda, YouTube, and Zoom links, please visit www.suttonma.gov.

Present in person: W. Stanhope, W. Talcott, R. Largess Jr., M. Gagan, Dave Mason, Associate (acting as full member)

Present remotely: none

Absent: E. McCallum

Staff: J. Hager, Community Development Director

## Action Items

ANR Plans – none

### 39 Gilmore Drive – Review of Site Plan Waiver – Schneider cross-dock for BJs

Attorney Henry Lane of Lane & Hamer was present with his client Cameron Pace of Smithfield, RI, representing Cowan Systems, a subsidiary of Schneider Trucking. He stated his client would like to lease 39 Gilmore Drive as a cross-dock pallet consolidation facility for BJs. The main warehouse and distribution is located in Uxbridge. This facility will receive pallets of goods from BJs stores where they were no fully sold or utilized, and re-pallet them as necessary for return to the main warehouse or re-routing to other stores. Goods received will be stored temporarily for varying amounts of time until re-palleted and shipped. It was noted that past issues included parking trucks and employee vehicles on Gilmore Drive and back up alarms in the middle of the night disturbing residents along Barnett Road. Mr. Pace stated they will need to make minor interior renovations to create a large dispatch area along with a few other minor adjustments within the front office portion of the building. There will be no changes to the warehouse or exterior of the building. The facility will employ 14 people, and approximately 40 trucks and/or cabs will leave and return to the facility daily. The facility will operate 24 hours. R. Largess Jr. asked if trucks operating out of this facility will pay excise taxes to Sutton. Mr. Lane stated they currently pay excise to Uxbridge, but have advised Cowan/Schneider that it would be appreciated if excise for the trucks regularly in Sutton was paid to Sutton. Mr. Pace stated most of their vehicles do not have back up alarms so they have no issues with a related restriction, he added there will be no outside company vehicles using the site.

Motion: To waive site plan review and allow the use of 39 Gilmore Drive as a cross-dock warehouse and distribution facility for BJs operated by Cowan/Schneider subject to the following conditions: 1) approval of all other necessary local and state permitting authorities 2) backup alarms will not be utilized on the site between 9 PM and 6 AM 3) no parking of any kind on Gilmore Drive and 4) the applicant/operator will return to the Board to resolve any issues that arise with the number of truck trips and/or traffic safety, R. Largess Jr.

2nd: M. Gagan

Vote: 5-0-0, D. Mason – aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, W. Talcott – aye, M. Gagan – aye

### ADU (Accessory Dwelling Unit) – proposed bylaw article minor adjustment

J. Hager explained in that their review of the entire Warrant, Town Counsel pointed out that the Use Table also needed to change the use reference from Accessory Apartments to Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Units and Large Accessory Dwelling Units per the proposed bylaw changes. This was the only change to the proposed bylaw recommended by the Board at their last meeting.

Motion: To recommend that Town Meeting approve the ADU article with the slight administrative change adjusting the Use Table to correctly reference the re-named use, R. Largess Jr.

2nd: D. Mason

Vote: 5-0-0, D. Mason – aye, R. Largess Jr. – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, W. Talcott – aye, M. Gagan – aye

### 128, 141 & 142 Armsby Road (Wedgewood Farm) – Review of Site Plan Waiver and roadway modification

Randy Waterman of WDA Design Group/Compton Property Development Inc. was present to review proposed amendments with the Board. He noted the project was approved back 2020. For six years he has been marketing the project and ensuring all permits are legally extending. Unfortunately, Covid caused issues, supply chain issues, rising price of construction, and interest rates have challenged the project. While quite a few developers have seriously considered the project, a few things keep coming up that need to be adjusted. The first is that triplexes need to have sprinklers and the middle units aren't worth as much/aren't as marketable as end units. The second is the roadway lengths and related cost. He asked the Board to allow the conversion of the 9 triplexes to 8 duplexes and 7 singles. For the time being he will lose 4 units. The second request was to change the roads that loop around units in the northwest and southeast units to cul-de-sacs with units to either side. This will reduce the length of pavement by about 1,000 feet and reduce land disturbance adding about a half-acre of green space. The Fire Department has already reviewed this roadway configuration. He noted he will likely return in the future to request adjustment to the Special Permit and Site Plan to add back the 4 lots units plus more. J. Hager stated she had a conversation with Jeff Walsh of Graves Engineering who stated he didn't have any particular concerns with the conversation of triplexes to duplexes and singles as the area of disturbance is likely very close and would likely not require significant grading changes. Nor did he have concerns with the roadway changes, but noted this change may involve more grading and drainage adjustments. Although this was not a public hearing, The Chair allowed questions from the public. R. Nunnemacher of 24 Singletary Avenue asked why Mr. Waterman chose to use loop roads in the original design. Mr. Waterman noted the loop roads with the gathering areas interior to all units is New Urbanist design. It's meant to bring people together. Unfortunately, now it is also pricier. He also responded to Mr. Nunnemacher that the project is likely to be constructed in four phases. He confirmed Wilkinsonville Water has committed to the necessary water, and he will provide revised plans to the Assessor's Office so they can re-number units accordingly. Andrea Mattei of 21 Golf Ridge Drive asked if all phases of the project will be under one condominium declaration. Mr. Waterman stated yes, they would be. She also questioned whether there would be a benefit of a public hearing process for those interested in the project. J. Hager stated a hearing is not a base requirement for Site Plan Review or amendments, this is simply Sutton's practice. In this case there is no increase in the number of units and an actual decrease in pavement/impact. M. Gagan stressed he would think abutters would welcome these adjustments, but in any case the changes are more technical in nature with no new impacts. D. Mason asked why not just come for all changes at once? Mr. Waterman stated he has current interested parties so he would like to get the smaller changes approved ASAP. As new or additional units will require much more engineering and a full hearing process, he will pursue these changes some point in the future. It was noted the additional units won't require changes to the layout or infrastructure of the existing project.

Motion: To grant a waiver of the formal Site Plan Review hearing process to allow triplexes to be converted to duplexes and singles and two of the four roadways to be converted to cul-de-sacs conditioned on the submission of fully engineered plans for the areas of the project that will be adjusted. Once reviewed and approved by the Town's consulting engineer, the proponent will return to the Board for their review and approval in open meeting, W. Talcott

2nd: R. Largess Jr.

Vote: 5-0-0, D. Mason – aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, W. Talcott – aye, M. Gagan – aye

## Administrative Items

### Minutes

Motion: To approve the minutes of 8/17/26, R. Largess Jr.

2nd: W. Talcott

Vote: 5-0-0, D. Mason – aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, W. Talcott – aye, M. Gagan – aye

Filings for October 5 – none currently, but possibly a scenic roadway/public shade tree hearing.

### Site Visit Reports

- 12 Pleasant Valley Road (Chipotle) – Reports from Graves Engineering regarding ongoing construction.

### Notices of Interest (3)

- Uxbridge – temporary moratorium on data centers
- Northbridge – prohibition on data centers
- Uxbridge – battery energy storage system (remanded back to Uxbridge as this use is a protected use)

J. Hager noted that she has also provided the Board with the September 8, 2026 Executive Order from the Governor regarding Data Centers as well as the related Statement of Expectations published on June 25, 2026. She noted as Sutton has a permissive bylaw, any use not listed is not allowed. Therefore, unless the Zoning Enforcement Officer feels data centers fit into one of the current uses allowed in Sutton, there is no need to panic and react without full knowledge. She stated she will be providing the Board and residents with information from reputable sources about data centers and their impacts so that if a proposed project comes forward the Board and the Town can make a more informed decision. In response to a question from W. Talcott, she stated unlike Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), data centers are not a protected use that all communities must allow.

### Correspondence

- Wilkinsonville Water District – Draft Water Management Act Permit for 100k more flow & commentary - J. Hager stated while the Town has no control over the three quasi-public water districts that operate within Sutton, they are critical to the financial and environmental health of Sutton. Two of the three districts are overseen by three Commissioners who are local residents and are run daily by a contracted operator, currently Whitinsville Water, who is also Sutton's third water district. The Town was happy to partner with the District's engineer to obtain mitigation credits necessary for this flow request. Input provided to DEP by J. Hager on the draft permit noted the Town had adopted the requested floor drain bylaw. DEP has already reviewed the bylaw and noted the District will receive additional mitigation credits for this effort. It remains to be seen how the Commissioners will reserve or allocate the additional 100,000 gpd flow when the permit is issued.

### Other Board Business

J. Hager noted there are concerns from Mr. Giamei who lives on Boston Road about Unified trucks on Boston Road. This will be scheduled for the next meeting to discuss including the conditions placed on truck traffic through the Unified Parkway approval process.

Motion: To adjourn, R. Largess Jr.

2nd: W. Talcott

Vote: R. Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Talcott – aye, W. Stanhope – aye, D. Mason - aye

Adjourned 8:30 pm
